question: Mia is “helping” her mom pick up \(30\) toys that are strewn on the floor. Mia’s mom manages to put \(3\) toys into the toy box every \(30\) seconds, but each time immediately after those \(30\) seconds have elapsed, Mia takes \(2\) toys out of the box. How much time, in minutes, will it take Mia and her mom to put all \(30\) toys into the box for the first time?
solution:
Track the number of toys just after Mom finishes each 30-second interval, before Mia removes any. After the first interval, this count is \(3\).

Between successive such moments, Mia removes \(2\) toys and Mom puts in \(3\), so the count increases by \(3-2=1\). The counts are therefore \(3,4,5,\ldots,30\). Reaching \(30\) requires \(30-3=27\) additional intervals, for a total of
\[
1+27=28
\]
intervals. Since each interval is half a minute, the time is
\[
28\cdot\frac12=14\text{ minutes}.
\]
All toys are in the box at that moment, before Mia's next removal. The answer is \(\boxed{14}\) minutes, choice B.

nodes.description: Identify arithmetic patterns (including patterns in the addition table or multiplication table), and explain them using properties of operations . For example, observe that 4 times a number is always even, and explain why 4 times a number can be decomposed into two equal addends.
nodes.label: 3.OA.D.9

nodes.description: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules. Identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms. Form ordered pairs consisting of corresponding terms from the two patterns, and graph the ordered pairs on a coordinate plane. For example, given the rule “Add 3” and the starting number 0, and given the rule “Add 6” and the starting number 0, generate terms in the resulting sequences, and observe that the terms in one sequence are twice the corresponding terms in the other sequence. Explain informally why this is so.
nodes.label: 5.OA.B.3

nodes.description: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself. For example, given the rule “Add 3” and the starting number 1, generate terms in the resulting sequence and observe that the terms appear to alternate between odd and even numbers. Explain informally why the numbers will continue to alternate in this way.
nodes.label: 4.OA.C.5

nodes.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide.* Examples: If 6 × 4 = 24 is known, then 4 × 6 = 24 is also known. (Commutative property of multiplication.) 3 × 5 × 2 can be found by 3 × 5 = 15, then 15 × 2 = 30, or by 5 × 2 = 10, then 3 × 10 = 30. (Associative property of multiplication.) Knowing that 8 × 5 = 40 and 8 × 2 = 16, one can find 8 × 7 as 8 × (5 + 2) = (8 × 5) + (8 × 2) = 40 + 16 = 56. (Distributive property.) *Students need not use formal terms for these properties.
nodes.label: 3.OA.B.5
